heading_en: Requirements for Observation of Real Prices
summary_ja: リスク・ファクターのモデル化可能性テストの実施と、用いる実在価格の要件・種類・文書化を定める。
summary_en: Requires the risk factor modellability test, and sets the requirements, permitted types and documentation for the real prices used in it.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall conduct the risk factor modellability test on the risk factors identified pursuant to the preceding Article and classify them into modellable risk factors and non-modellable risk factors; provided, however, that where necessary in light of conditions in financial or capital markets and other circumstances, it may change the classification of a risk factor that failed the risk factor modellability test to a modellable risk factor, but only where it has notified the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency in advance.

In the risk factor modellability test, real prices that fall under either of the following requirements shall be used. (i) All of the following requirements are satisfied, and at least 24 observations of real prices are identified in the most recent twelve months. (a) At least four observations of real prices exist in any 90-day period within the most recent twelve months. (b) The identification of real price observations is limited to one per day. (c) Whether the requirements in (a) and (b) are satisfied is monitored once a month. (ii) At least 100 observations of real prices (limited to one per day) are identified in the most recent twelve months.

A real price shall be any of the following prices; provided, however, that prices referred to in collateral exchange relating to margin (meaning variation margin prescribed in Article 123, paragraph (1), item (xxi)-10 and initial margin prescribed in item (xxi)-11 of that paragraph of the Cabinet Office Order on Financial Instruments Business, etc. (Cabinet Office Order No. 52 of 2007)) shall not be included in real prices. (i) The price of a transaction conducted by the company itself. (ii) The price of an actual transaction conducted between third parties (limited to those whose price can be verified as appropriate). (iii) A price referencing a committed quote (meaning a price certified by a third-party vendor (meaning a provider of information on financial transactions other than the Ultimate Designated Parent Company and its consolidated subsidiaries, etc.; the same applies hereinafter in this Article), an exchange (meaning a financial instruments exchange prescribed in Article 2, paragraph (16) of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act, a similar foreign institution, or a commodity exchange; the same applies hereinafter) or a trading platform (meaning a mechanism similar to a third-party vendor or an exchange that provides information on financial transactions); the same applies in the following item). (iv) A price obtained from a third-party vendor that satisfies either of the following requirements. (a) It is a committed quote and transaction price collected by that third-party vendor. (b) The company has agreed with the third-party vendor to submit documents evidencing the committed quotes and transaction prices upon request of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency. (c) It falls under any of the prices referred to in the preceding three items.

Where real prices falling under item (iv) of the preceding paragraph are used, all of the following requirements shall be satisfied. (i) Information on the number of observations and the observation dates of those real prices can be obtained from the third-party vendor. (ii) Information necessary to confirm the association with the risk factor can be obtained from the third-party vendor. (iii) The third-party vendor is subject to external audit with respect to those real prices, and has agreed with the company to submit the results of that external audit upon request of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall prepare a document stating the information necessary to judge the appropriateness of the real prices used in the risk factor modellability test and of the procedures for associating those real prices with risk factors.
